newsitem.title: USA: Oneida Cty, N.Y., $71.4 mln GOs single-A - Fitch.
newsitem.headline: Oneida Cty, N.Y., $71.4 mln GOs single-A - Fitch.

text.p: Oneida County, NY.'s $71.4 million outstanding general obligation bonds are rated 'A' by Fitch Investors Service.

The uncertain outlook has been removed. The rating reflects the county's moderate debt levels, improved financial performance and economic stabilization since the closures at the Griffiss Air Force Base.

The county has taken sound measures to improve its financial performance. By imposing an additional one-cent sales tax in fiscal 1992, the county has achieved positive operating results for five consecutive years, including a projected surplus in 1996. At fiscal year end 1995, the general fund balance was $11.3 million, or 6.3% of expenditures.

The unreserved, undesignated fund balance was $5.5 million, or 3.0% of expenditures. The partial closure of the Griffiss Air Force Base, the county's largest employer, and the full closure of the Lockheed Martin facilities have resulted in the loss of approximately 2,700 nonmilitary jobs. However, new service and other jobs created in the county helped offset these losses.

The Oneida Nation casino, opened in 1993, currently employs 2,036 workers and a Wal-Mart distribution center, opened in 1994, employs 1,563 workers. Accordingly, unemployment rates have dropped from previous highs in 1992, while the labor force has remained stable.

The unemployment rate for the county in September 1996 was 4.4%, compared to 5.7% for the state and 5.2% for the nation. Income levels are below state and national indicators, which is typical of upstate communities. Debt levels are moderate at $776 per capita and 2.6% of market value of the taxable property base. The county's five-year capital improvement plan totals $45.3 million, $34.5 million of which will be funded through future debt issuance.
